blocks.title: Global warming and the greenhouse effect
blocks.text: Global warming is the long-term rise in the earth's average surface temperature due to human activities, primarily the emission of greenhouse gases (GHGs) from burning fossil fuels. The progressive warming of the earth's surface by the blanketing effect of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere is the greenhouse effect (Figure 14.5).

blocks.alt: A block of land with trees, tall buildings and a factory with chimneys under the sun. Solid yellow arrows labelled Sunlight come down to the ground; a dashed arrow labelled Reflected sunlight goes back up to the label Energy released back into space. Dashed arrows rise from the ground and the buildings to the gases CH4, CO2, SF6 and N2O, under the label Greenhouse gases (trap heat), and come back down. The label Energy absorbed is on the ground.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 14.5 lists NO2 among the greenhouse gases; the greenhouse gas is N2O (nitrous oxide), as drawn above.

It is a global-scale problem of air pollution. Carbon dioxide and water vapour transmit short-wavelength solar radiation but reflect back the longer-wavelength heat radiation from the warmed surface of the earth. The greenhouse effect depends on the ability of these gases to absorb infrared radiation: by day heat from the sun passes through the atmosphere and warms the earth; at night the earth radiates heat towards space, and some atmospheric gases trap that heat, preventing its loss. The higher the concentration of carbon dioxide and the other gases, the greater the absorption of thermal radiation and the greater the rise in global temperature.
Name the greenhouse gases and explain how they cause global warming.
